title: 10 · Exception Handling (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: the safety net

A trapeze artist works over a net. Code that might fail (a missing file, dividing by zero) is the trapeze; the exception handler is the net. An exception is an event at run time that breaks the normal flow. Unhandled, the program crashes and prints a stack trace. Handled, you show a friendly message and carry on.

try, catch, finally

try holds the risky code. catch (Type e) runs only if that type of problem occurs. finally runs always (cleanup like closing files), error or not. A try needs at least one catch or a finally. e.getMessage() gives the error text. If an exception occurs, the rest of the try block is skipped.

Multiple catches

Java checks catches in order and runs the first match. Put specific types first and general (Exception) last; the other order will not compile because the specific block becomes unreachable. Since Java 7 you can combine with catch (A | B e).

Common exceptions

ArithmeticException: int divide by zero. NullPointerException: using a null reference. ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: bad index. NumberFormatException: Integer.parseInt("abc"). ClassCastException: bad cast. InputMismatchException: Scanner expected a number. FileNotFoundException and IOException: file problems. SQLException: database problems.

The hierarchy

Throwable splits into Error (serious, do not catch, e.g. OutOfMemoryError) and Exception. Under Exception, RuntimeException and its children are unchecked; everything else (IOException, SQLException) is checked.

Checked vs unchecked

Checked: verified at compile time; you must handle (try/catch) or declare (throws). Unchecked: happen at run time; handling is optional (they usually mean a bug to fix).

throw vs throws

throw triggers an exception inside a method body: throw new IllegalArgumentException("Age cannot be negative");. throws declares in the signature that a method may pass a checked exception to its caller: void read() throws IOException.

Custom exceptions

Extend Exception (checked) or RuntimeException (unchecked) and pass a message up with super: a class named InsufficientFundsException. This ties inheritance to exceptions.

try-with-resources and best practice

Resources opened in the try parentheses are closed automatically in reverse order. Best practice: catch specific types, never leave a catch empty, handle only what you can actually fix, and clean up in finally or with try-with-resources.

lab.task: Write readAge(String text) that converts text to int and throws IllegalArgumentException if it is below 0 or above 120. In main call it with 'abc', '-5' and '30', handling NumberFormatException and IllegalArgumentException separately, with a finally that prints 'checked'.
